And when I load the app in my browser I get: 

An error has occurred

Does anyone know what it is trying to do with 'su' to start a worker? And ideas why it would fail?

Thanks,
Tristan

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Error: su: must be run from a terminal
parts:
Despite the misleading error message, the problem here is indeed that Shiny Server expects to be run with root privileges.

This is because Shiny Server was originally designed to allow all users (or all users in a certain group) on the server to host Shiny apps themselves, and their apps would execute with their permissions. We use su to drop privileges when spawning the R process (rather than simply fork/setuid/exec), since it knows all the subtleties about doing so, e.g. which environment variables need to be dropped/changed, the right incantation to setgid/initgroups, etc.

Shiny Server still allows you to do this (it's the autouser mode) but with the other two modes of operation, "site directory" (the default) and "direct mapping", it's easy to imagine the Shiny Server process running as a particular user and all the spawned R processes running as the same user. Other than listening on port <1024 there would be no inherent need to run as root. But Shiny Server doesn't detect that case right now.

I didn't think about the PaaS case--that is a particularly good reason for us to remove the run-as-root restriction. I'll see if I can take care of this.

We use su to drop privileges when spawning the R process (rather than simply fork/setuid/exec), since it knows all the subtleties about doing so, e.g. which environment variables need to be dropped/changed, the right incantation to setgid/initgroups, etc.

Shiny Server still allows you to do this (it's the autouser mode) but with the other two modes of operation, "site directory" (the default) and "direct mapping", it's easy to imagine the Shiny Server process running as a particular user and all the spawned R processes running as the same user. Other than listening on port <1024 there would be no inherent need to run as root. But Shiny Server doesn't detect that case right now.

I didn't think about the PaaS case--that is a particularly good reason for us to remove the run-as-root restriction. I'll see if I can take care of this.
